title: U.S. House · Virginia's 1st District
area: Virginia's 1st Congressional District (Northern Neck, Middle Peninsula, and parts of Fredericksburg-area and Hampton Roads exurbs)

context.text: The Republican primary was canceled and incumbent Robert J. Wittman advanced unopposed. Shannon Taylor won the Democratic primary on August 4, 2026 with 53.0% of the vote in a seven-candidate field.

summary.text: Robert J. "Rob" Wittman is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Virginia's 1st District, first elected in a 2007 special election after about 26 years in Virginia state government and service in local and state office. He sits on the House Armed Services and Natural Resources Committees. His official biography emphasizes military and veterans' issues, the Chesapeake Bay, infrastructure, and rural broadband.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C. in 1959. According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, he grew up in Henrico County, where his mother taught school and his father had served in the Army in World War II.

Holds a bachelor's degree in biology from Virginia Tech (1981), a master's degree in health policy and administration from the University of North Carolina (1990), and a Ph.D. in public policy and administration from Virginia Commonwealth University (2002).

Spent 26 years in Virginia state government before Congress, working as an environmental health specialist for local health departments in the Northern Neck and Middle Peninsula and later as field director of the Virginia Health Department's Division of Shellfish Sanitation.
Won his first race in 1986 for the Montross Town Council, serving 10 years, four of them as mayor.
Was elected to the Westmoreland County Board of Supervisors in 1995 and became its chairman in 2003.
Was elected to the Virginia House of Delegates (99th District) in 2005 and served until his election to the U.S. House in 2007.

Has represented Virginia's 1st District since 2007. His official biography lists him as vice chairman of the House Armed Services Committee and chairman of its Tactical Air and Land Forces Subcommittee, as a member of the Natural Resources Committee and the Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party, and as co-chair of the Congressional Shipbuilding Caucus and the Chesapeake Bay Watershed Caucus.
His official biography says his Serving Rural America Act served as a model for the NTIA Broadband Infrastructure Program, and that he serves on the U.S. Naval Academy's Board of Visitors.
According to his Ballotpedia survey, he and his wife, Kathryn, have lived in Montross since 1985 and have two children and six grandchildren.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources as Vice Chair, and on the House Committee on Armed Services, chairing the Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittee, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Serves on the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Shannon Taylor
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 53.0% of the vote

summary.text: Shannon Taylor is the Commonwealth's Attorney for Henrico County and the Democratic nominee for Virginia's 1st District. She has been Henrico's chief prosecutor since 2012 and ran unsuccessfully for the 2025 Democratic nomination for Virginia Attorney General. She is campaigning on congressional ethics reform, including bans on stock trading and lobbying by members of Congress, alongside lowering costs for families.

background.text: Born in 1967 and an alumna of Albemarle High School, according to Wikipedia and Ballotpedia.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Virginia in 1989 and a law degree from the University of Richmond School of Law in 1995.

Elected Henrico County Commonwealth's Attorney in November 2011, winning an open contest after the incumbent suspended his bid for a fifth term; she is the first woman to hold the office. She took office in January 2012.

Describes herself, in her 2025 Ballotpedia survey, as the first Democrat elected Commonwealth's Attorney for Henrico County in over 20 years, and says she has won re-election three times with bipartisan support.

The Henrico County website says her office, with a staff of 80, prosecutes cases in Circuit Court, General District Court, and Juvenile and Domestic Relations Court. According to her campaign website, as quoted by Ballotpedia, her office has a 90% homicide conviction rate.

In her Ballotpedia surveys, describes establishing programs to support victims of human trafficking, a task force on the opioid epidemic, and efforts to take illegal guns off the streets, and says she was one of the first prosecutors in the nation to push back against criminalizing women and doctors for accessing abortions after Roe was overturned.
Ran for the Democratic nomination for Virginia Attorney General in 2025, losing the June 17 primary to Jay Jones 51.1% to 48.9%.
Won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary for Virginia's 1st District with 53.0% of the vote in a seven-candidate field.

priorities.text: Proposes mandatory jail time of at least one year for members of Congress who misuse at least $10,000 in taxpayer funds, and a lifetime ban on members of Congress becoming lobbyists for industries they regulated.
Proposes a ban on members of Congress trading individual stocks while in office and pledges to refuse corporate PAC contributions.
Says she will fight to restore expired Affordable Care Act subsidies and expand Medicare's ability to negotiate prescription drug prices.

positions.summary: Says she will fight to restore Affordable Care Act subsidies and expand Medicare's ability to negotiate directly with pharmaceutical companies.
positions.quote: I will fight to restore the Affordable Care Act subsidies that Rob Wittman allowed to expire and restore funding for rural hospitals.

sources.title: Shannon Taylor's campaign website, quoted by Ballotpedia (June 25, 2026)

researchNotes: No campaign website content or public statements of policy positions were located directly for Robert Wittman for this cycle within the research budget; his record reflects official committee assignments only. Taylor's stock-trading and net-worth figures about Wittman on her campaign site are her own campaign claims, not independently verified here, and are reported as her stated position rather than as fact. A biography page on Shannon Taylor's campaign site could not be loaded; her biography relies on Henrico County's official page, her Ballotpedia survey responses, and Wikipedia, so her pre-2012 career is not described.
